title: Dinosaurs Are Older Than FLOWERS 🌸
description:
Quick, guess what's older: dinosaurs, or your flowers? Dinosaurs, by almost a hundred million years. Stegosaurus probably never saw a single flower: just ferns, and green, and more green. No wonder it ate the bouquet. But T. rex? Flowers everywhere. And T. rex lived closer in time to YOU than to Stegosaurus!
Dinosaurs or flowers: what did you guess?

The science: the first definite dinosaurs appear in rocks about 230 million years old (Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor, from Argentina's Ischigualasto Formation, about 231 to 228 million years old). The oldest fossils that are definitely from flowering plants are pollen grains about 140 to 133 million years old (from Italy and Israel), and the oldest fossil flowers about 130 to 125 million years old. Molecular clocks and a few disputed older pollen grains hint that flowering plants began earlier, so this goes by the oldest flowers ever found. Stegosaurus lived about 155 to 145 million years ago, among ferns, cycads, conifers and horsetails (a disputed Jurassic "flower" from China is why we say probably). By the end of the age of dinosaurs, flowering plants were everywhere: about 9 in 10 of the leaf species in the Hell Creek rocks, where T. rex is found, are from flowering plants. T. rex lived about 68 to 66 million years ago, so about 80 million years separate it from Stegosaurus, and only about 66 million separate it from you. Bonus: the last dinosaurs did meet grass: bits of it turned up in fossil dinosaur dung from central India (Prasad et al., Science, 2005).
